sources.source_title: PostgreSQL unaccent extension behavior on Turkish dotless-ı and dotted-İ
sources.source_url: internal: direct SQL query against oryn-qa-scratch, `select unaccent('...')`
sources.claim_supported: unaccent('Kırıkkale') = 'Kirikkale', unaccent('İSTEK Okulları') = 'ISTEK Okullari' -- the database-side convention that lib/acquisition/normalize.ts's dbNormalizedName() is documented to match and, per this session's testing, does not
sources.limitations: Reflects this specific Postgres instance's unaccent extension version/rules file as installed on oryn-qa-scratch; not independently verified against a second Postgres instance, though unaccent's default rules file is standard/stable across installs.

sources.source_url: internal: throwaway Node scripts run this session, replicating lib/acquisition/normalize.ts's nameKey()/dbNormalizedName() verbatim
sources.claim_supported: U+0130 (İ) has a canonical NFD decomposition to U+0049+U+0307 (confirmed, correcting this session's own initial wrong hypothesis); U+0131 (ı) has no decomposition and is deleted/splits words under nameKey()'s ASCII-only alnum-fold step
sources.limitations: Verified against this session's exact copy of the two functions' current source; if either function is edited after this research lands, results should be re-verified against the new version rather than assumed to still hold.

sources.source_title: PostgreSQL unaccent extension behavior on German ß (eszett) and apostrophe characters
sources.source_url: internal: direct SQL query against oryn-qa-scratch, `select unaccent('Weißensee')`
sources.claim_supported: unaccent('Weißensee') = 'Weissensee' (confirms ß->ss folding, the same mechanism gap as Turkish ı, in dbNormalizedName()); unaccent() does not touch apostrophe characters at all (confirms the apostrophe-style finding is not a JS/DB disagreement, unlike ı/ß)
sources.limitations: No live canonical_entities row containing ß was found to test end-to-end (checked, zero matches) -- this finding is mechanism-verified and defensive, not evidence of a currently-manifested duplicate the way the Turkish ı finding is.

sources.source_title: ROR API direct records for Purdue University (system and West Lafayette campus) and Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
sources.source_url: https://api.ror.org/v2/organizations/05p8z3f47, https://api.ror.org/v2/organizations/02dqehb95, https://api.ror.org/v2/organizations/05vt9qd57 (fetched via curl, not WebFetch -- WebFetch returned a socket error against this API in this session)
sources.claim_supported: Purdue: ror.org/05p8z3f47 is the multi-campus 'Purdue University System' parent; ror.org/02dqehb95 ('Purdue University West Lafayette') is the correct, more specific child entity ORYN's rows should map to. Rutgers: only one ROR entity exists (ror.org/05vt9qd57) for the entire university -- no separate New Brunswick/Newark child, unlike ORYN's own two-row split.
sources.limitations: Confirms current ROR state as of the retrieval date only -- ROR records can change (new child entities added, relationships revised).

sources.source_title: ROR API direct records for Université de Franche-Comté / Université Marie et Louis Pasteur / Université Bourgogne Franche-Comté / Université Bourgogne Europe, and Université Toulouse III - Paul Sabatier / Université de Toulouse
sources.claim_supported: Université de Franche-Comté's ROR record is status='inactive' with a direct successor relationship to Université Marie et Louis Pasteur (est. 2024), itself one of two successors to the 2015-2024 Université Bourgogne Franche-Comté federation. Université Toulouse III - Paul Sabatier is a direct predecessor of Université de Toulouse (est. 2025). Both are real, current, recent French university mergers/renames -- see 04-rename-history-framework.md.
sources.limitations: Confirms current ROR state as of the retrieval date only. This session did not independently verify these mergers against each institution's own official French-language announcement/decree -- ROR's own status/relationship fields are treated as sufficient evidence for an open registry per this package's source standard (00), but a fully primary-source confirmation (e.g. the French ministerial decree) was not separately fetched.
